questions.title: A twenty-place circular queue
questions.statement: A program stores positive integers in a circular queue. Declare a global one-dimensional array Queue of 20 integers, each initialised to -1. Initialise global HeadPointer and TailPointer to -1 and NumberItems to 0. Write Enqueue(InputData): return False if the queue is full; otherwise store the integer at the next position, update the pointers and count, and return True. The main program must call Enqueue() for every integer from 1 to 25 in ascending order. Output one line for each integer, such as "5 Successful" when stored or "23 Unsuccessful" when full. Write Dequeue(): return -1 if the queue is empty; otherwise return the next item and update the pointers and count. Extend the main program to call Dequeue() twice and output each return value. Save your source and a screenshot of the run for teacher review.

questions.title: Separate data into six colour files
questions.statement: Use the supplied TheData.txt, which contains 72 comma-separated integer and colour records. The six supplied colour files start empty. Write ReadData() to prompt for a filename and return an array of raw text lines, without assuming a fixed number of lines. SplitData(DataArray) must separate each integer into one of six colour arrays and call StoreData for each array and its matching filename. StoreData(DataToStore, FileName) must append each item on a new line and handle file errors. In the main program, call ReadData() and pass its returned array to SplitData(). Run the program with TheData.txt and retain the resulting Red.txt content for teacher review.

stages.title: ReadData: filename prompt and raw lines
stages.description: Prompt for a filename; read an unknown number of lines into a 1D array and return it.

stages.title: SplitData: six colour arrays
stages.description: Accept DataArray, split each raw line and place its integer in the matching colour array.

stages.title: StoreData: append and file errors
stages.description: Accept DataToStore and FileName, append items line by line and handle opening or writing errors.

stages.title: Store all six colour arrays
stages.description: Within SplitData, call StoreData once for each colour array with its matching filename.

stages.title: Main program
stages.description: Call ReadData(), then pass its result to SplitData(). Run with TheData.txt.

stages.title: Run and file evidence
stages.description: Teacher reviews the run record and the generated Red.txt content. Evidence marks do not block automatic AC.

questions.title: A binary tree built with classes
questions.statement: Use object-oriented programming to build a binary tree of integers. Declare Node with attributes NodeData (integer), LeftNode (Node or null) and RightNode (Node or null). Its constructor receives the integer data and sets both links to null. Add GetLeft(), GetRight(), GetData(), SetLeft(Node) and SetRight(Node). In the main program, create five Node objects holding 10, 20, 5, 15 and 7 in that order. Declare Tree with a FirstNode attribute, a constructor that receives its root Node and a GetRootNode() method. Write Insert(NewNode) so smaller values travel left, while equal or larger values travel right, repeating until the new node can be linked. Write a recursive OutputInOrder(RootNode) function or Tree method to print the node values in ascending order. Extend the main program to create the Tree with the 10 node, insert the other four nodes in the order given, then call OutputInOrder() with the root node. Your final program is checked automatically; the teacher may inspect the source and saved run when assigning stage marks.

stages.title: 3(a)(i) Node and constructor
stages.description: Declare Node and initialise its data and null links.

stages.title: 3(a)(ii) Get methods
stages.description: Return the left node, right node and integer data.

stages.title: 3(a)(iii) Set methods
stages.description: Store a Node object in each child link.

stages.title: 3(b) Five nodes in the main program
stages.description: Teacher checks that the main program creates Node objects containing 10, 20, 5, 15 and 7.

stages.title: 3(c)(i) Tree and constructor
stages.description: Declare Tree and initialise FirstNode from the Node argument.

stages.title: 3(c)(ii) GetRootNode
stages.description: Return the root Node object.

stages.title: 3(c)(iii) Insert a Node
stages.description: Find the correct parent, putting smaller data left and equal or larger data right.

stages.title: 3(d) Recursive OutputInOrder
stages.description: Automatic cases check output order for two trees. The teacher separately inspects the source to award marks for the recursive algorithm.

stages.title: 3(e)(i) Build and output the tree
stages.description: The main program must create the five Node objects in order, build the Tree, insert the four original objects in order and call OutputInOrder with the root.

stages.title: 3(e)(ii) Test evidence
stages.description: Teacher reviews the saved run output as evidence; a screenshot is optional.

Q2_a.driverCode:
try:
    import contextlib
    import importlib.util
    import io
    import sys
    from pathlib import Path
    
    output_names = ("Red.txt", "Green.txt", "Blue.txt", "Orange.txt", "Yellow.txt", "Pink.txt",)
    original_outputs = {name: Path(name).read_bytes() for name in output_names if Path(name).exists()}
    old_stdin = sys.stdin
    try:
        sys.stdin = io.StringIO('TheData.txt\n')
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
            spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('candidate', '/w/main.py')
            candidate = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
            spec.loader.exec_module(candidate)
    finally:
        sys.stdin = old_stdin
        for name, content in original_outputs.items():
            Path(name).write_bytes(content)
    def read_file(name):
        previous_stdin = sys.stdin
        prompt = io.StringIO()
        try:
            sys.stdin = io.StringIO(name + '\n')
            with contextlib.redirect_stdout(prompt), contextlib.redirect_stderr(prompt):
                data = candidate.ReadData()
        finally:
            sys.stdin = previous_stdin
        return data, prompt.getvalue()
    
    short, short_prompt = read_file('ShortData.txt')
    long, long_prompt = read_file('LongData.txt')
    _, missing_prompt = read_file('MissingData.txt')
    assert isinstance(short, (list, tuple)) and isinstance(long, (list, tuple))
    assert [str(item).rstrip('\r\n') for item in short] == ['10,red', '22,blue', '7,pink']
    assert len(long) == 80 and str(long[0]).rstrip('\r\n') == '1,red'
    assert str(long[-1]).rstrip('\r\n') == '80,red'
    assert short_prompt.strip() and long_prompt.strip()
    assert missing_prompt.strip() and missing_prompt.strip() != short_prompt.strip()
    print('OK')
except Exception:
    print('__CHECK_FAILED__')
